newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms to buy 40% stake in Chile copper mine.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms to buy 40% stake in Chile copper mine.

text.p: Nippon Mining and Metals Co said on Thursday that it and four other Japanese firms had signed a letter of intent to take a 40 percent stake in Chile's Los Pelambres copper mine.

The companies did not disclose the amount of money they had paid for their stake in the mine, which plans to expand copper output by 260,000 tonnes per year by September 1999. The expansion will cost $1.3 billion.
The Japanese investors will be divided into two groups, one consisting of Nippon Mining, with a 15 percent stake, Marubeni Corp with 8.75 percent, and Mitsui & Co Ltd with 1.25 percent.
The other group will consist of Mitsubishi Materials Corp with 10 percent and Mitsubishi Corp with five percent.

The groups also signed a long-term contract with Los Pelambres for the purchase of copper concentrates, with 250,000 tonnes of concentrates for the Nippon mining group, and 150,000 tonnes for the Mitsubishi group.
The letter of intent was signed with Antofagasta Holdings Plc, whose mining division Minera Anaconda is developing the mine.
Los Pelambres, which currently produces 23,000 tonnes of copper per year, has reserves of 2.4 billion tonnes of ore with a grade of 0.63 percent copper, Nippon Mining said.
Work on the expansion is scheduled to begin in July this year, with completion due in September 1999. Nippon Mining expects the formal contract to go into effect aorund mid-1997.
